extra.message: The database setup wizard builds SQL by string substitution: each user-controlled argument (database name, database username, generated/attacker-supplied password) is inserted into the statement with replacedSql.replaceFirst("\\?", arg) and only semicolons are stripped (arg.replace(";", "&#094")). The resulting string is executed with connection.createStatement().executeUpdate(replacedSql). Sources are request parameters read in doPost (e.g. openmrs_new_database_name at line 618, create_database_username at line 622) or derived from them (connectionUsername at 1464). Quote/backtick payloads allow breaking out of the quoted/backticked SQL context (e.g. create database `?`, create user '?'@...), causing SQL injection.

Setup-wizard request parameters are written into the Velocity model unescaped and rendered directly into HTML attributes. InitializationFilter.java reads attacker-controlled values such as httpRequest.getParameter("database_connection") (line 589) and httpRequest.getParameter("openmrs_new_database_name") (line 618) into wizardModel, and this template emits them as value="${databaseConnection}" with no HTML escaping (EscapeTool/esc is not configured in velocity.properties). A value like "><script>alert(document.cookie)</script> is reflected back and executed, giving reflected XSS on the pre-authentication setup pages. Same pattern in remotedetails.vm:17 (${remoteUrl}), databasesetup.vm:54/78/89, implementationsetup.vm and others.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The testing-install flow fetches an attacker-supplied URL. testConnection(urlString) calls new URL(urlString).openConnection() with no scheme/host allow-list, and createConnection(url) does the same before POSTing base64 credentials to it. urlString comes from httpRequest.getParameter("remoteUrl") (InitializationFilter.java:818) and flows through getResourceInputStream. This permits SSRF to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, and file: URLs during setup.

User-supplied input selects a class and field to load/read via reflection. addConceptReference(String ref) (line 141) passes any reference containing a '.' to evaluateStaticConstant, which calls Context.loadClass(clazzName), clazz.getDeclaredField(constantName) and field.get(null) with attacker-chosen class/field names and setAccessible(true). getConceptByReference(conceptRef) (ConceptServiceImpl.java:359, ConceptService.java:377) is a public API with no privilege annotation, so externally-controlled strings can force loading/initialization of arbitrary classes (running their static initializers) and read arbitrary static fields (information disclosure).

cwe: CWE-470: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection')

extra.message: Polymorphic Jackson typing with JsonTypeInfo.Id.CLASS (@class) allows an attacker to control which class is instantiated during deserialization. EntityEvent payloads are persisted to the outbox_event table and later deserialized by OutboxPollingTaskHandler.java:107-113 using Context.loadClass(item.getEventType()) followed by objectMapper.readValue(item.getPayload(), eventClass). If the event type/payload can be influenced (persisted rows, broker input), this is arbitrary type instantiation / gadget-chain deserialization.

readChangeLogResource(resourceName) creates a dom4j SAXReader and calls reader.read(is) without disabling DOCTYPE/external entities, unlike readChangeLogFile (lines 141-144) which sets disallow-doctype-decl and disables external general/parameter entities. An XML document containing an external entity is therefore parsed with external entity resolution enabled, enabling XXE (local file disclosure / SSRF) when the parsed content can be influenced.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: getTempData(String key) resolves the caller-supplied key against the JVM temp directory with Path tempDir.resolve(key) and then opens it via Files.newInputStream(tempFile), with no normalization or containment check (contrast LocalStorageService.getPath/assertKeyInStorageDir, which validate against the storage dir). A key containing ../ sequences reads arbitrary files under the temp root. This is part of the public StorageService API (StorageService.java:51).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Hardcoded default AES key and initialization vector (ENCRYPTION_VECTOR_DEFAULT = "9wyBUNglFCRVSUhMfsTa3Q==", ENCRYPTION_KEY_DEFAULT = "dTfyELRrAICGDwzjHDjuhw==") are used by Security.getSavedInitVector()/getSavedSecretKey() (Security.java:312-321, 344-353) whenever the encryption.vector / encryption.key runtime properties are not configured, and then feed Security.encrypt/decrypt (AES/CBC, Security.java:228-288). Data encrypted with these publicly-known constants is trivially decryptable, and the static IV is reused.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
